ui_bugs.issue: document.querySelector('link[rel=canonical]') on /blog/<slug> returns 'https://vehiq.pl/' (root) instead of the per-post canonical 'https://vehiq.pl/blog/<slug>'. document.title IS updated correctly via Helmet, but the canonical <link> from /index.html is not being replaced by the Helmet canonical. Likely root cause: react-helmet-async only updates Helmet-managed nodes — the static <link rel="canonical" href="https://vehiq.pl"> in /app/frontend/index.html stays in <head> and is the only canonical at runtime. Fix options: (a) remove the static canonical from /app/frontend/index.html so Helmet's becomes authoritative, OR (b) add a top-level Helmet (e.g. in App.js / public layout) that sets a default canonical and is then overridden per-route. Affects Blog list (https://vehiq.pl/blog) AND BlogPost (per slug) — both currently appear as canonical = https://vehiq.pl/ in DOM.

Share counter increment is gated on navigator.clipboard.writeText() success. If clipboard write throws (denied permission / non-secure context / headless test env) the catch silently returns and the POST /api/vehicles/public/<slug>/share is never called, so share_count does not increment. UX-wise: a user who clicks Share intending to share but clipboard fails would also not register a share. Recommend: fire the share API regardless (best-effort) OR before the clipboard attempt, then handle clipboard errors separately. Tested manually: backend share endpoint works fine via direct POST.

issues: Eye/Share2 icons and number sit too close to the units label, e.g. '5views' / '3shares' have no space between digit and label in the DOM text content. Likely a missing space/whitespace span between number and the translated unit. Looks fine visually due to flex gaps but copy/paste/screen-reader output is unfriendly.

Make POST /api/vehicles/public/<slug>/share fire independently of clipboard success in PublicVehicle.js copy() (avoid losing share counts when clipboard denied).

routers/blog.py admin_create accepts payload.published flag and stamps published_at — clean. admin_update only stamps published_at the FIRST time published flips to true (keeps original publish date on re-publish). Good behavior.

routers/blog.py public list_published projects {_id:0, content:0} but then sets content='' in _public_post wrapper — efficient, but the wrapper hard-codes content key in returned dict; consider a separate _list_post serializer to make the contract explicit.

routers/vehicles.py track_public_view uses unique index on (vehicle_slug, session_id, date) — DuplicateKeyError is caught and dedupe works as designed. RC: privacy.profile_visible==false returns 404 (good). However the bare `except Exception:` swallows ALL errors silently — a real DB outage would look like a successful counted=false. Consider catching only pymongo.errors.DuplicateKeyError.
routers/vehicles.py track_public_share has no dedupe — per spec (anonymous-safe, raw count). Idempotency on share is acceptable per requirement.
Frontend BlogPost.js readingTime() only counts plaintext words via /\s+/.split — does not strip Markdown punctuation; minor inaccuracy on heavily-formatted posts (cosmetic).
Frontend AdminBlog.js (not viewed in depth) — assume editor wires save-draft to POST /api/admin/blog with published:false and publish to POST/PATCH. Verified via UI test toast 'Utworzono draft'.

Frontend PublicVehicle.js uses optimistic share count bump (setShareCount(c=>c+1)) before API resolves — fine for UX but combined with the clipboard-failure issue above means user may see an incremented number locally while backend was never called (no — actually, the optimistic bump is INSIDE the try block AFTER navigator.clipboard.writeText, so it only runs when clipboard succeeds; correct).
Helmet integration: index.html has a static canonical that is not removed by react-helmet-async. Document this as a known limitation: Helmet appends nodes but does NOT clean static head tags.

rca of the issue: Canonical override: index.html ships a static <link rel=canonical href="https://vehiq.pl">. react-helmet-async appends Helmet-managed nodes but does not always remove static head links with the same rel. Net result: at runtime the canonical link DOM element is still the one from index.html, so document.querySelector('link[rel=canonical]').href === 'https://vehiq.pl/' regardless of Helmet's per-page setting. Fix: delete the static canonical from /app/frontend/index.html (or set a Helmet defaultProps in App.js with a placeholder canonical that Helmet can subsequently override per-page).
